# hostd_vm (Resource)

A Public Cloud virtual machine. Creation waits until the VM is running. If that call is interrupted, a VM with the same hostname that appeared during the call is kept instead of creating another; an existing VM with that hostname is never adopted. Destroying stops the VM, deletes its disks, and deletes all of its backups. Public addresses return to the pool unless `retain_public_ips` is true (a reserved IPv4 stays billed). Changing `project_id`, `hostname`, `os_image`, `username`, `wan_ip`, or `wan_ipv6` replaces the VM. For a production VM set `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. CPU, RAM, disk, CPU class and networking can be changed in place. Lowering CPU or RAM requires `power_state` `stopped` and is refused until 24 hours after create or the last increase. Import with `<project_id>/<vmid>`; `os_image`, `ssh_key_ids` and `username` are create-time inputs the API does not return. After an import, set `os_image` and `ssh_key_ids` in the configuration (they are recorded without replacing the VM) and omit `username`. A VM that was paused outside Terraform is resumed or stopped to match `power_state`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hostd_vm" "web" {
  project_id  = hostd_project.main.id
  hostname    = "web-01"
  os_image    = "debian-12-amd64.qcow2" # a name from data.hostd_os_images
  ssh_key_ids = [hostd_ssh_key.admin.id]
  cores       = 2
  ram_gb      = 4
  os_disk_gb  = 20

  # Destroying this VM deletes its disks and every backup of it.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

output "web_ipv4" {
  value = hostd_vm.web.ipv4
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cores` (Number) vCPU count (even numbers from 2), within the account CPU quotas.
- `hostname` (String) DNS-style hostname (letters, digits, hyphens and dots; at most 64 characters).
- `os_disk_gb` (Number) OS disk size in GiB, in steps of 20 GiB; between 10 and 100 GiB per vCPU. It cannot shrink.
- `os_image` (String) Image name available in the project, e.g. `debian-12-amd64.qcow2`. List the available names with the `hostd_os_images` data source.
- `project_id` (String) UUID of the project (`hostd_project`) the VM belongs to.
- `ram_gb` (Number) RAM in GiB; between 1 and 4 GiB per vCPU.
- `ssh_key_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of SSH keys (`hostd_ssh_key`) to install, from one to five. The VM is reached with these keys: the provider sets a random cloud-init password and does not expose it. Keys are installed only when the VM is created. A later change is recorded without touching the VM, so rotating or renaming a `hostd_ssh_key` never replaces it; update `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the guest yourself.

### Optional

- `cpu_mode` (String) CPU class: `light` or `regular` (default).
- `lan_interfaces` (Attributes List) Private networks to attach. `mode` `auto` takes a free address; `select` uses `ip`. When `wan_mode` is `off` and more than one network is attached, set `is_gateway` on exactly one. Create the networks in the portal first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lan_interfaces))
- `power_state` (String) `running` (default) or `stopped`. `stopped` shuts the guest down. Set it to `stopped` to lower CPU or RAM. The API also refuses that downgrade until 24 hours after the VM is created or CPU, RAM, or CPU class is increased.
- `retain_public_ips` (Boolean) When destroying the VM, or turning public networking off, keep its public addresses reserved in the project. A reserved IPv4 stays billed. Defaults to false, which releases the addresses.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `username` (String) Cloud-init username. Defaults to the OS image's default user.
- `wan_ip` (String) Reserved project IPv4 to attach. Omit to take the next free address. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `wan_ipv6` (String) Reserved project IPv6 to attach. Omit to take the next free address. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `wan_mode` (String) Public network: `off`, `ipv4`, `ipv6` or `dual` (default). With `off`, attach at least one private network. Switching between `ipv4`, `ipv6` and `dual` requires going through `off`.

### Read-Only

- `ipv4` (String) Public IPv4 address, empty when none is attached. Stays known in the plan while `wan_mode` does not change.
- `ipv6` (String) Public IPv6 address, empty when none is attached. Stays known in the plan while `wan_mode` does not change.
- `vmid` (Number) VM identifier (VMID) assigned by the API.

<a id="nestedatt--lan_interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `lan_interfaces`

Required:

- `mode` (String) `auto` or `select`.
- `vnet` (String) Private network name (VNet).

Optional:

- `ip` (String) IPv4 address. Required when `mode` is `select`.
- `is_gateway` (Boolean) Use this network as the default gateway. Required on exactly one interface when WAN is off and several networks are attached.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for creation and for `power_state`. Defaults to 10 minutes.
- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the VM to stop and be deleted. Defaults to 10 minutes.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for a resize, shutdown, or start. Defaults to 15 minutes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import hostd_vm.web 0b6e5f7c-4f4e-4a43-9c0e-6f4d3b2a1c90/104
```
